newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money trade quiet, banks resort to c.bank.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money trade quiet, banks resort to c.bank.

text.p: Croatian money market rates were mostly flat on Tuesday with some bank lenders cutting their prices in quiet trade, dealers said.
But they saw demand as likely to pick up in mid-week due to the corporate profit tax payment with an April 30 deadline.
"We thought this might cause more banks to withdraw earlier placements and to affect trade today. But it did not," dealer Jasenka Blagaic told Reuters.
The situation may have been helped by the banking sector taking out Lombard loans from the central bank. These are granted at 9.5 percent for 12 days a month.
One large bank borrowed 30 million kuna this morning. Banks ended Monday borrowing 74.5 million kuna in Lombard funds to square their positions, the central bank said.
Blagaic put money market settlements at a meagre 19.2 million kuna by 1030 local (0830 GMT), leaving over 20 million surplus on the supply side.
Call money was steady at 10.5 percent and insurers' one-week rate at 9.0 percent.
Some interbank term rates edged down as foreign banks with good kuna liquidity granted one-month loans at 13 percent.
This compares to 15 percent recently or 16 charged to poorly regulated savings-credit institutions, considered to carry a greater risk of repayment.
Savings banks paid 14.5 percent for two-week funds.
